title: Pistachio and Cardamom Shortbread Cookies
story: No eggs, no leavening, just butter, flour, powdered sugar, and cardamom. Shortbread doesn't need much help. Cardamom and pistachio have been a reliable combination for a few thousand years, so the flavor is sorted. The fork crosshatch takes two seconds. Don't skip it.

items.text: ½ cup unsalted butter, at room temperature

steps.text: Whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, ½ cup powdered sugar, 1 tsp ground cardamom, and ½ tsp fine salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat ½ cup room-temperature butter until smooth and creamy, about 1–2 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Butter should look pale and fluffy and hold a soft peak when you pull the beater away.

steps.text: Add the dry ingredients to the butter and mix until just combined. The dough will look crumbly at first — keep mixing until it comes together into a smooth dough.
Fold in ¼ cup finely chopped pistachios.
Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and place them 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet.
Flatten each ball slightly with the palm of your hand, then press a fork lightly into the top to make a crosshatch pattern.

steps.donenessCue: Edges should be just barely golden — the tops will stay pale. Shortbread doesn't brown the way other cookies do. Pull them when the edges look set and dry; overbaking makes them hard instead of tender.

steps.text: Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. They're fragile while warm. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt while still warm if using.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Toast the pistachios in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2–3 minutes before chopping — the flavor deepens significantly.
Add ½ tsp rose water to the butter before adding the dry ingredients. A little goes a long way; it rounds out the cardamom without taking over.
Roll the dough into a log, wrap in parchment, and refrigerate for 1 hour, then slice into rounds instead of rolling into balls — cleaner edges and a more uniform cookie.
Press a whole pistachio into the center of each cookie before baking instead of the crosshatch — simpler and more visually distinct.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week — shortbread keeps better than most cookies. Freeze baked cookies for up to 3 months; thaw at room temperature.
